questions.question: Who were the Wright brothers, and how did their work before 1903 help them build an aeroplane?
questions.expected_answer: Wilbur and Orville Wright were brothers from the United States who ran a bicycle shop in Dayton, Ohio. Building and repairing bicycles taught them about light, strong machines and balance. They studied birds, read about flight, built gliders and tested them at Kitty Hawk.

questions.question: Name three problems of flight the Wright brothers solved and how they solved each.
questions.expected_answer: Control: they invented wing warping, twisting the wings like birds do. Lift: they built a wind tunnel and tested about two hundred wing shapes. Power: they built their own light engine with their mechanic Charlie Taylor and designed their own propellers.

questions.question: What happened on 17 December 1903, and when was the first flight in South Africa?
questions.expected_answer: Orville Wright flew the Flyer at Kill Devil Hills, near Kitty Hawk, for 12 seconds and 37 metres, the first powered, controlled flight. That day, there were four flights, and the longest, by Wilbur, lasted 59 seconds. The first flight in South Africa was by Albert Kimmerling in East London on 28 December 1909.
